复合命题由基本命题和「若……则……」「并且」等连接词构成。在经典命题逻辑中，复合: A compound proposition is built from atoms and connectives such as “if … then …” and “and”. In classical propositional logic, its value is determined by the values of its atoms. A truth table lists every assignment and result: n distinct atoms give 2ⁿ assignments.
条件命题 X → Y 只在 X 为真、Y 为假时为假；前件 X 为假时，它按定义: The conditional X → Y is false only when X is true and Y false. When its antecedent X is false, the conditional is true by definition. This connective is material implication; it does not assert that X causes Y.
在<wiki-ref to=\"truth\"></wiki-ref>的每一行都: A proposition true on every row of its is a tautology, for example “it rains → it rains” or “it rains ∨ ¬it rains”. Consistently substituting propositions for its atoms preserves validity.
穷举真值表可以判断命题逻辑公式是否为永真式，但 n 个基本命题需要检查 2ⁿ 行: A complete truth table decides whether a propositional formula is a tautology, but n atoms require 2ⁿ rows. A proof instead derives its conclusion using rules, without enumerating each row.
要说明一个命题不是<wiki-ref to=\"tautology\"></wi: To show a proposition is not a , one truth assignment making it false suffices; this is a counterexample. One counterexample refutes validity, but failure to find one is not by itself a proof.
对于没有前提的命题，只要找到使它为假的真值组合，就能排除它在可靠系统中的无前提证: For a proposition with no premises, an assignment making it false rules out a premise-free proof in a sound system. When premises are present, a counterexample must also make every premise true.
连接词将较小的命题组成复合命题：¬（非）、∧（与）、∨（或）、→（若……则……）: Connectives form compound propositions from smaller ones: ¬ (not), ∧ (and), ∨ (or), → (if … then …), and ↔ (if and only if). In classical propositional logic, their truth values are determined by their components, so they can be represented by logic gates.
在经典真值语义下，可以用「与」和「非」，或用「或」和「非」，表示这些连接词。证明: Under classical truth-value semantics, these connectives can be expressed using “and” and “not”, or using “or” and “not”. The prover supplies corresponding introduction and elimination rules.
在经典真值表的每一行都为假的命题称为<b>矛盾式</b>，例如「下雨 ∧ ¬下雨: A proposition false on every row of a classical truth table is a contradiction, for example “it rains ∧ ¬it rains”. The prover uses ⊥ as a distinguished false proposition; a contradictory formula is not necessarily syntactically identical to ⊥.
在本证明器中，¬A 定义为 A → ⊥。因此，证明 ¬A 可以通过假设 A 并从: In this prover, ¬A is defined as A → ⊥. To prove ¬A, one can assume A and derive ⊥.
一句话（或几句话一起）至少在一种情况下为真，叫<b>可满足</b>；一种都没有，: A sentence (or several together) is satisfiable when it is true in at least one case; when it is true in none it is a , also called unsatisfiable. In propositional logic a case is a row of the ; in first-order logic it is a world.
在经典命题逻辑中，A 是永真式当且仅当 ¬A 不可满足。基于反驳的证明方法会否定: In classical propositional logic, A is a tautology exactly when ¬A is unsatisfiable. Refutation-based methods negate the goal and check whether a satisfying assignment remains.
在经典命题逻辑中，若 A、B 在每个真值组合下同真同假，则二者<b>语义等价</: In classical propositional logic, A and B are semantically equivalent if they have the same truth value under every assignment. The biconditional A ↔ B states both implications and can be written (A → B) ∧ (B → A).
等价的两句可以互相替换：句子里哪一处换成和它等价的话，整句的真假都不变。化简器就: Equivalent sentences can stand in for each other: replace any part of a sentence with something equivalent and the whole keeps its truth. This is what the simplifier relies on to turn a sentence into another way of saying the same.
A → B 的<b>逆否命题</b>是 ¬B → ¬A：若下雨则地湿，那么地不湿: The contrapositive of A → B is ¬B → ¬A. From “if it rains, the ground is wet”, a dry ground rules out rain. The prover derives this direction using Apply and an assumption box.
仅由 A → B 不能一般性地推出其<b>逆命题</b> B → A，也不能推出: A → B alone does not generally imply its converse B → A or its inverse ¬A → ¬B; both inferences have counterexamples.
有了<wiki-ref to=\"contradiction\"></wiki-: From a ⊥ anything can be proved: the rule is often called the principle of explosion (Latin ex falso quodlibet). In the prover it is the part .
在经典真值语义中，前件为假的条件命题恒为真。证明器则通过矛盾消去规则从 ⊥ 推出: In classical truth-value semantics, a conditional with a false antecedent is true. The prover instead applies contradiction elimination to derive the desired conclusion from ⊥; this does not mean contradictory premises are true in reality.
由 A ∨ B 和 ¬A 得出 B，叫<b>选言三段论</b>，就是「排除法」。: From A ∨ B and ¬A, B: this is the disjunctive syllogism, the process of elimination. In the prover it is no rule of its own but a case split: the A side meets ¬A in ⊥, which goes to ; the B side is the conclusion already.
排中律 A ∨ ¬A 表示命题 A 或其否定成立。它是经典命题逻辑的永真式，但不: The law of excluded middle A ∨ ¬A states that A or its negation holds. It is a classical propositional tautology, but has no premise-free proof using this game’s intuitionistic rules alone. Adding double-negation elimination makes it provable; the result becomes <part-ref to="lemma:lem"></part-ref>.
<wiki-ref to=\"classical\"></wiki-ref>接受: <wiki-ref to="classical"></wiki-ref> accepts excluded middle; <wiki-ref to="intuitionistic"></wiki-ref> does not adopt it as a general principle.

Quantifiers too: ¬∀x. P(x) is equivalent to ∃x. ¬P(x), and ¬∃x. P(x) to ∀x. ¬P(x). Two of the directions, ¬(A ∧ B) → ¬A ∨ ¬B and ¬∀ → ∃¬, take proof by contradiction.
句子里没有 → 和 ↔，¬ 只贴在最小的句子上，叫<b>否定范式</b>。把 A: A sentence with no → or ↔, and every ¬ on a smallest sentence, is in negation normal form. Turn A → B into ¬A ∨ B, drop double negations, and push each ¬ all the way in with : every sentence comes to this shape, meaning the same.
先化成<wiki-ref to=\"nnf\"></wiki-ref>，再把「或: First , then distribute “or” over “and” until every “or” is under the “and”s: strings of “or” joined by “and”, the conjunctive normal form. Each string of “or” is a clause. Distributing makes a sentence longer, exponentially at worst; automatic provers often use another conversion (naming parts with new letters) to avoid it.
<wiki-ref to=\"cnf\"></wiki-ref>里的每一串「或」: Each string of “or” in the is a clause, and each item in it (a sentence or its negation) a literal. For a set of clauses to hold together, each clause needs at least one true literal. The empty clause has none and can never be true: it is ⊥.
<b>证明</b>是从前提、公理和推理规则出发的有限推导。每一步要么是允许的出发: A proof is a finite derivation from premises, axioms and inference rules. Each step is an allowed starting point or follows from earlier steps by a rule; checking rule applicability depends on formula structure.
命题真值表的行数随基本命题数量指数增长。形式证明可以利用一般规则和变量，建立适用: A propositional truth table grows exponentially in the number of atoms. A formal proof can use general rules and variables to establish a family of cases; reasoning about infinite domains still requires appropriate quantifiers and rules.
<b>推理规则</b>说明怎样从前提推导结论。例如，套用由 A → B 和 A: An inference rule specifies how conclusions follow from premises. For example, Apply derives B from A → B and A. Letters represent proposition schemata and can be consistently instantiated as the rule permits. On the proof board, inputs represent premises and the output represents the conclusion.
